clue.text: Untroubled as Gallio ?

parts.note: Gallio, the Roman proconsul in Acts 18, famously 'cared for none of those things', so he was free of worry

explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible Gallio dismissed the quarrel brought before him and 'cared for none of those things'; split the answer as CARE FREE and it describes him exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without worries is light-hearted and easygoing.

clue.text: Firm man, and convincing

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A steady chap who is persuasive.
explanation.definitionFit: A cogent argument is persuasive and compelling.

clue.text: Argue about a descendant

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a son is a descendant

explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to debate or put a case logically.

clue.text: What a professional man charges Herb for the freehold

parts.note: a fee is the charge made by a lawyer or doctor
a simple is an old word for a medicinal herb

explanation.surface: A lawyer bills someone called Herb for a property deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name; it is a herb, called a simple in old herbals.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, an estate held outright and inheritable without limit is the fullest form of property ownership, a freehold.

clue.text: Lady Godiva barely qualified as one

definitions.text: Lady Godiva barely qualified as one

parts.words: Lady Godiva barely qualified as one
parts.note: Godiva rode naked through Coventry, so 'barely' is literal: she was a woman on horseback with nothing on

explanation.walkthrough: 'barely' suggests only just; it means without clothes, as Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who rides horses, especially a circus performer on horseback, is a female rider.

clue.text: Be sure confusion reigns in a place of darkness

indicators.note: the words 'Be sure' are thrown into confusion, signalling their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Uncertainty rules in some gloomy underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion reigns in' rearranges BESURE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Erebus is the dark region of the underworld, personified primeval darkness.

clue.text: River named for a bumper

annotationWithheld.why: River named for a bumper: R + OUSE needs 'River' to give both R and the river OUSE; 'named' supplies no letters, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Scatters Webster's letters about

indicators.note: the letters of the word are moved about, signalling they are rearranged

parts.note: the name taken with its S, all eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone flings the dictionary's pages around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters about' rearranges WEBSTERS, with the possessive S counted as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestrew is to scatter things over a surface, to strew.

clue.text: Like Kate, hers perhaps is to desire

indicators.note: suggests the word may be in another form, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to wish is to desire

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges HERS into SHRE. Kate is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Katherina is the bad-tempered shrew of the play, so ill-tempered and nagging describes her.

clue.text: " Belial, in act more —— and humane " (Milton)

definitions.text: Belial, in act more —— and humane " (Milton)

parts.words: Belial, in act more —— and humane " (Milton)
parts.note: a line from Paradise Lost Book II with one word blanked out, which the solver supplies

explanation.walkthrough: Milton's line describing the fallen angel Belial reads 'in act more graceful and humane'; the answer is the word missing from the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank describes Belial's elegant bearing, a word meaning elegant in movement.

clue.text: He is often at sea with his accounts

definitions.text: He is often at sea with his accounts

parts.words: He is often at sea with his accounts
parts.note: 'at sea' suggests muddled with the books, but literally means aboard ship, where one officer keeps the ship's money

explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the idiom for being confused; here it is literal: the ship's officer in charge of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's officer who handles the finances and passengers' money serves on board, keeping the vessel's books.

clue.text: Stanley was the very model of a modern kind

definitions.text: Stanley was the very model of a modern kind

parts.words: Stanley was the very model of a modern kind
parts.note: Gilbert and Sullivan's Stanley sings 'I am the very model of a modern' senior army officer

explanation.walkthrough: In The Pirates of Penzance Stanley's patter song is 'I am the very model of a modern Major-General'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley in the operetta holds a senior army rank, just below lieutenant general.

clue.text: She returns to complain to one

indicators.note: the word for complaining comes back, so it is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: to complain is to moan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A woman goes back to grumble to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' looks like the subject of 'returns'; it is the definition, a woman's name, and 'returns' is the reversal signal for the complaining word only.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, Ruth's mother-in-law in the Bible, so a female pronoun covers her.

clue.text: An alarming figure of a man!

definitions.text: An alarming figure of a man!

parts.words: An alarming figure of a man!
parts.note: the figure is literally a man-shaped dummy whose job is to alarm birds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a frightening person; the figure is a straw dummy set up in a field to frighten crows.
explanation.definitionFit: A farmer's stuffed effigy in old clothes is put in fields to scare birds off crops.

clue.text: One bird goes about selling others

parts.note: a sparrow is a bird
to hawk goods is to go about peddling them

explanation.surface: A bird peddles its wares to other people.
explanation.walkthrough: The first bird plus a verb for peddling makes the name of other birds: the definition is just 'others', meaning other birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparrowhawks are small birds of prey, different birds from the first one named.

clue.text: Light sequel to the " Bee's Wedding ""?

definitions.text: Light sequel to the " Bee's Wedding ""?

parts.words: Light sequel to the " Bee's Wedding ""?
parts.note: the holiday after a wedding, with 'light' as the moonlight and the bee providing a sweet syrup

explanation.walkthrough: A bee's product plus the light of the night sky gives the trip after a wedding; 'The Bees' Wedding' is a Mendelssohn piano piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The newly-weds' holiday comes right after the wedding, a sweet first month.

clue.text: A disc jockey has a small sum nearby

parts.note: a cent is a small sum of money

explanation.surface: A radio presenter keeps a little money close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying next to, neighbouring.

clue.text: Wolfgang's bevy of wives

explanation.walkthrough: Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera Die Entführung aus dem Serail is known in English as Il Seraglio.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera about an abduction from a harem, and the women's quarters of a sultan's palace holding his wives and concubines.

clue.text: Powerful contrivance of genie in Leeds perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the letters given may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A magical spirit in a Yorkshire city as a mighty device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges GENIEINLEEDS. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A compression-ignition motor is a powerful machine driving lorries and locomotives.

clue.text: It plays its part in certain shootings

definitions.text: It plays its part in certain shootings

parts.words: It plays its part in certain shootings
parts.note: shootings here are film or photo shoots, not gunfire

explanation.walkthrough: 'shootings' suggests guns; it means filming or photography.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that takes photographs or films is what one 'shoots' a scene with.

clue.text: Pierre's article is on one style of singing

parts.note: Pierre is French, and un is the French indefinite article
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's essay is about a choral method.
explanation.walkthrough: Pierre stands for any Frenchman, so his 'article' is the French a, UN.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means all voices on the same melody together.

clue.text: Greek king, the Brow ing version

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Browning translated Aeschylus's tragedy about this king in 1877; 'The Browning Version' is also the title of Rattigan's play in which that translation features.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the Mycenaean ruler who led the Greeks against Troy, and Browning published a translation of the Aeschylus tragedy named after him.

clue.text: Heather makes a rice concoction.

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture, signalling these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone named Heather cooks a rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; it is the plant. 'concoction' rearranges ARICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths, the shrubby plants of moorland.

clue.text: Long for a story about the east

indicators.note: the word for a story goes round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a yarn is a story
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Craving a tale set in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside YARN.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long, to pine or crave something.

clue.text: Eat this cake like lightning

parts.note: the French word for lightning names a pastry, which one might also bolt down quickly

explanation.walkthrough: The pastry's name is French for 'lightning', perhaps because it is eaten in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: An éclair is a long choux pastry filled with cream and topped with chocolate; the French word means a flash.

clue.text: Imprecatory cavalrymen, they say

parts.note: imprecatory means given to cursing, and the proverb says one swears like these mounted soldiers

explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'swear like a trooper' makes these cavalry soldiers the proverbial cursers.
explanation.definitionFit: Troopers are private soldiers in a cavalry or armoured regiment, proverbial for foul language.

clue.text: Uncharacteristic of him, no doubt

parts.note: the apostle known for doubting the resurrection, so having no doubt would be out of character

explanation.walkthrough: The apostle who would not believe until he saw the wounds is 'Doubting' Thomas, so 'no doubt' does not suit him.
explanation.definitionFit: The disciple called Doubting for his scepticism would find certainty untypical.

clue.text: Scheme with volunteers in to produce 'plant

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plan involving volunteers yields a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army (TA) is Britain's part-time volunteer reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a herb of roadsides and lawns, or a banana-like tropical crop.
